Projects prevalences of disability with an estimated model

Source: R/predict.prevalence_model.R
predict.prevalence_model.Rd

Calculates prevalences by age and year from a model estimated with fitPrevalenceModel.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'prevalence_model'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  interval = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  on_unfeasible = c("warn", "clip", "error"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a model estimated with fitPrevalenceModel

newdata

a data frame with variables 'year', 'age' (+ 'qx' for method "mortality") and, optionally, the variables defining series

interval

if TRUE, adds the lower and upper bounds of a prediction interval ('pix_lwr' and 'pix_upr')

level

confidence level of the prediction interval

on_unfeasible

method "target" only: what to do if the hypothesis cannot be satisfied with the projected mortality, i.e. if it requires prevalences outside the interval 0 to 1 (all ages) or if no uniform evolution can reach the target (minimum age). "warn" (default) returns the values as they are with a warning (prevalences outside the interval 0 to 1, or NA for a uniform evolution without solution); "clip" bounds prevalences to the interval 0 to 1 (or to the closest feasible solution), with a warning; "error" stops.

...

not used

Value

the rows of newdata with a new variable 'pix' (projected prevalence), and 'pix_lwr' and 'pix_upr' if requested. If the scale of the model is "log" or "level", prevalences are bounded to the interval 0 to 1 (with a warning).

Details

With methods "trend" and "shift", newdata only needs the years and ages. With method "mortality", newdata must also contain the mortality rates 'qx' for all the ages of the model and for each year (they are used at ages \(a+k\), see fitPrevalenceModel). Variables defining series (sex, categories) can be omitted from newdata: it is then used for all the values of these variables in the model (for example, mortality rates by sex apply to all categories). Rows of newdata with ages that are not in the model are dropped.

Prediction intervals (with interval = TRUE) are calculated on the scale of the estimation, from the residual variance of the regression, and then transformed back to prevalences. They do not take into account the uncertainty on the projected mortality rates, nor the uncertainty on the validity of the model outside the period of estimation. They are not available for estimator = "endpoints", nor for methods "target" and "shift".

See also

fitPrevalenceModel, projectPrevalence

Examples

ages <- 60:100; years <- 2010:2019
obs <- expand.grid(age = ages, year = years)
obs$pix <- plogis(-6 + 0.12 * (obs$age - 60) - (0.01 + 0.0005 * (obs$age - 60)) * (obs$year - 2019))
m <- fitPrevalenceModel(obs, method = "trend")
proj <- predict(m, newdata = expand.grid(age = ages, year = c(2025, 2030)), interval = TRUE)
head(proj)
#>   age year         pix     pix_lwr     pix_upr
#> 1  60 2025 0.002328964 0.002328964 0.002328964
#> 2  61 2025 0.002617277 0.002617277 0.002617277
#> 3  62 2025 0.002941177 0.002941177 0.002941177
#> 4  63 2025 0.003305027 0.003305027 0.003305027
#> 5  64 2025 0.003713722 0.003713722 0.003713722
#> 6  65 2025 0.004172744 0.004172744 0.004172744
